summary: Ahijah foretells the ruin of Jeroboam’s house, the death of his child, and the scattering of the Israelites because of their idolatry—Jeroboam dies and Nadab reigns—Judah, under Rehoboam, turns to wickedness—Shishak of Egypt takes treasures from the temple—Rehoboam dies and Abijam reigns.
meta_description: Ahijah foretells the ruin of Jeroboam’s house, the death of his child, and the scattering of the Israelites because of their idolatry—Jeroboam dies and Nadab reigns—Judah, under Rehoboam, turns to wickedness—Shishak of Egypt takes treasures from the temple—Rehoboam dies and Abijam reigns.

footnotes.note15_d: HEB asherim; i.e., idolatrous, wooden poles, pillars, or trees. Deut. 16:21.
footnotes.note19_a: It is significant that the kings of Israel and Judah kept official records; these records are no longer extant; they were used as source books by the author(s) of our books of Kings; they are not our books of Chronicles.
footnotes.note24_a: HEB male prostitutes; devotees of idolatrous, paganistic fertility worship.
footnotes.note31_a: OR Abijah (see 2 Chr. 12:16) or Abia (see Matt. 1:7).
